<reason>Both sides fought a genuinely sharp, narrowing debate. A's core route was that "meaningful human control" is undefinable and unverifiable, so a ban only disarms the compliant; the Ottawa/cluster-munitions signatory turn ([A2.1]) was A's best moment, converting B's own examples into evidence of verification failure, and the fog-of-war parity on accountability ([A2.3], [A4.1]) blunted B's "no author" line to a real degree. But B controlled the decisive clash. B drew the line A said could not be drawn (defensive munition-intercept envelopes vs systems selecting human beings in open environments) and held it consistently, including squarely accepting that loitering munitions are covered. B's Q2 then forced A to name a restraint surviving its own objection, and A's answer — mandatory human review of context before any engagement against personnel, enforced by certification — handed B the closing collapse: that is the motion's rule, and a certification you must pass is a deployment prohibition on failing it. A's reply (verify a presence vs prove an absence) is the best available escape and is a real distinction in enforcement architecture, but it concedes the substantive principle the motion asserts, and B had pre-empted it by noting audit logs are written by the same software A distrusts. A also left B's escalation/flash-crash and proliferation-of-doctrine arguments essentially unanswered, and misdescribed B as never drafting the Phalanx exception when B had. A's Q1 did expose a real tension in B's cheap-proliferation vs industrial-supply-chain framing, and B's staged answer was only adequate; B also incurred a genuine execution cost with two turns clipped over the word cap, losing its asymmetry punchlines. Net: B's path to victory survived intact and B made the choice easier to resolve.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's closing move on [A4.2]: pressing A to name an enforceable restraint, then showing A's proposed "mandatory human review of context before any engagement against personnel" is precisely meaningful human control — so A spent four speeches denying the line existed and then drew it in the same place. A's prohibition-vs-certification distinction was a credible but partial escape.</best_rebuttal>
